title: arxiv_2304.05170v2
universal_lens: Multi-object tracking in sports scenes unifies motion dynamics and appearance discrimination via probabilistic association kernels. Multi-object tracking datasets exhibit scene-specific motion and appearance regimes; SportsMOT distinguishes via fast, variable-speed player dynamics with similar yet identifiable attire.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference on player trajectories integrates motion likelihood with appearance posterior for robust tracking in GSI. Bayesian tracking inference in SportsMOT leverages appearance-motion dual likelihoods, conformally calibrated for robust object identity across occlusion and high-speed transitions.
gse_mapping: Situation-aware state transitions in GSE model player motion and visual identity using hybrid kinematic-appearance logic gates. Situational reasoning in GSE models SportsMOT dynamics through state-transition graphs encoding player velocity, posture variability, and jersey-number distinctiveness for real-time tracking.

primitives.verbatim_quote: Our dataset is characterized with two key properties: 1) fast and variable-speed motion and 2) similar yet distinguishable appearance.
primitives.assumptions: Players exhibit non-linear motion patterns; visual features are partially overlapping but discriminable.

primitives.name: MixSort Framework Architecture
primitives.verbatim_quote: To alleviate the issue, we further propose a new multi-object tracking framework, termed as MixSort, introducing a MixFormerlike structure as an auxiliary association model to prevailing tracking-by-detection trackers.
primitives.assumptions: Auxiliary models enhance primary tracker's association capability through cross-modal feature fusion.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When primary tracker fails due to ambiguous motion or appearance, auxiliary model provides fallback.

layer2.mapping: MixSort's dual-model architecture maps to GSI's ensemble inference kernel for robustness.
layer2.telemetry: Performance gain in MOT metrics when auxiliary model is active.

The empirical validation on SportsMOT underscores the necessity of addressing both motion variability and appearance ambiguity in real-world sports analytics.
